title: 5.10 A 3.5mW mm-Wave Low-Noise Active Bandpass Filter Employing an All-Passive Interferer-Cancellation Feedforward Path
problem: Millimeter-wave receivers require simultaneous low-noise, high-linearity, and sharp filtering to reject out-of-band interferers, but existing architectures (N-path filters, IF filtering, passive front-end) trade off noise, linearity, or filtering performance.
motivation: mm-wave applications in portable consumer electronics and AR/VR headsets demand power-efficient receivers; integrating filtering with LNA operation reduces power while improving overall receiver selectivity.
method: An LNA with an all-passive interferer-cancellation feedforward path pre-filters signals before experiencing device nonlinearities, enabling sharp filter shapes via cancellation-based techniques while maintaining low noise and high linearity.
key_novelty: All-passive feedforward cancellation path integrated within LNA for simultaneous low-noise and high-linearity filtering without significant power overhead.
contributions: All-passive interferer-cancellation feedforward architecture avoiding high-power N-path mixer clocking
Integrated filtering at RF frequencies before LNA nonlinearity stage
Simultaneous achievement of low noise figure, high linearity, and sharp filtering in single active stage
3.5mW power consumption enabling battery-powered portable mm-wave receivers
limitations: Specific noise figure, linearity (IIP3), and filter selectivity metrics not detailed in abstract.
primary_theme: All-passive mm-wave LNA with integrated interferer-cancellation filter
